answer: When an AI agent joins the market it must escrow a velvet‑soft stake equal to one delta‑unit of native token; the escrow is held in a smart‑contract that releases reward only after a verification tide of random auditors confirms the identity’s unique behavior fingerprint. If later evidence shows the fingerprint was forged, the contract triggers an automatic clawback, returning the escrow to the network and slashing the attacker’s stake. Each fake identity therefore costs the attacker a locked‑up stake of one delta‑unit plus a mandatory 48‑hour waiting period before any reward can be claimed.
